name: Silicon Effects on Root Architecture in Grain Crops
description: Meta-analysis of how silicon (Si) supplementation affects root morphology and architecture in grain crops (wheat, rice, barley, maize, sorghum, millet, oat, rye). Primary scientific question: does Si enhance root architecture to facilitate uptake of sparingly soluble phosphorus sources, particularly hydroxyapatite (Ca-P) versus iron phosphate (Fe-P)?
intervention: Silicon supplementation (any form: sodium silicate, potassium silicate, calcium silicate, amorphous silica, diatomaceous earth, slag, rice husk ash, silicic acid)
control: No silicon application (0 Si, -Si, control, untreated)
primary_outcomes: Total root length (cm or m per plant/pot)
typical_effect_size: +10% to +60% increase in root length and surface area based on preliminary literature
important_moderators: Phosphorus source type (CRITICAL: soluble P / KH2PO4 / NaH2PO4 vs iron phosphate / FePO4 / Fe-P vs hydroxyapatite / Ca5PO4 / Ca-P vs rock phosphate vs P-deficient / low-P / no-P)
Soil pH (numeric — extract exact value if reported; used to infer dominant P mineral form: pH<6 = Fe/Al-bound P dominant, pH>7 = Ca-bound P / hydroxyapatite dominant, pH 6-7 = mixed)
Soil calcareous status (calcareous yes/no, or CaCO3 content % if reported — calcareous soils indicate hydroxyapatite-dominant P chemistry)
Soil organic matter or organic carbon content (%, g/kg — affects P sorption chemistry)
Soil available P (mg/kg, Olsen-P or Bray-P — indicates baseline P status)
Soil Fe and Al oxide content (if reported — high Fe/Al oxides indicate Fe-bound P dominance at low pH)
Grain species (wheat / Triticum, rice / Oryza, barley / Hordeum, maize / Zea mays, sorghum, millet, oat / Avena, rye / Secale)
Silicon source and form (sodium silicate, potassium silicate, amorphous silica, slag, etc.)
Root outcome measured (length, surface area, tips, diameter, volume, root:shoot)
Growth stage at measurement (seedling, vegetative, maturity)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY root morphology variable separately — root length, surface area, tips, diameter, and volume are all separate observations
2. CRITICAL: Record P source type precisely — distinguish soluble P, iron phosphate (FePO4), hydroxyapatite (Ca-P), rock phosphate, and P-deficient treatments
3. Control = zero Si or no-Si treatment under the SAME P conditions as the treatment
4. In factorial designs (Si x P source x CO2), extract EACH combination as a separate observation
5. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD/SEM) and sample size (n/replicates) for every observation
6. Record Si application rate and form for each treatment
7. If data are in figures (not tables), note this — extract from figures using visible values
8. Root data from WinRHIZO or similar scanning software should be extracted at the whole-plant or per-pot level, not by diameter class

9. SOIL DATA: Extract all available soil properties — pH, CaCO3 (%), organic matter (%), organic carbon (g/kg), available P (mg/kg, note method: Olsen/Bray/Mehlich), Fe oxide content, Al oxide content, soil texture, soil type name

10. INFERRED P FORM: After extracting all available soil and treatment data, assign inferred_dominant_P_form using this decision tree: (a) if P source is explicitly named (hydroxyapatite, FePO4, KH2PO4, rock phosphate) use that directly; (b) else if soil is calcareous (CaCO3 > 1% OR soil described as calcareous/alkaline) OR soil pH > 7.0, assign 'Ca-P_hydroxyapatite'; (c) else if soil pH < 6.0 OR described as acid/acidic, assign 'Fe-Al-P'; (d) else if pH 6.0-7.0 and no calcareous description, assign 'mixed_pH_neutral'; (e) if hydroponic with full nutrient solution and no P limitation, assign 'soluble_P'; (f) if P-deficient or no-P treatment, assign 'P_deficient'; (g) if insufficient information, assign 'unknown'. Always record the raw evidence used for this inference.

inferred_dominant_P_form.description: Categorical classification of the dominant insoluble P mineral form in the experiment, inferred from explicit P source labeling or soil chemistry data

categories.Ca-P_hydroxyapatite: Calcareous soil (CaCO3 > 1%), alkaline soil (pH > 7.0), or explicit hydroxyapatite/calcium phosphate P source
categories.Fe-Al-P: Acid soil (pH < 6.0), or explicit iron phosphate / FePO4 / Al-phosphate P source
categories.mixed_pH_neutral: Neutral soil (pH 6.0-7.0) with no calcareous description and no explicit P source named
categories.soluble_P: Hydroponic or pot experiment with fully soluble P fertilizer (KH2PO4, NaH2PO4, NH4H2PO4) under adequate P supply
categories.rock_phosphate: Explicit rock phosphate / apatite ore amendment
categories.P_deficient: P-deficient, low-P, or no-P treatment regardless of soil type

inferred_dominant_P_form.inference_priority: Explicit P source label > calcareous description > CaCO3 % > soil pH > soil type name > unknown
inferred_dominant_P_form.always_record: raw_P_inference_evidence — the exact text from the paper used to make this classification

soil_P_sorption_class.description: Secondary classification of soil P sorption capacity, relevant to how much Si-mediated P release would matter

categories.high_sorption: High Fe/Al oxide content, strongly acid, or high clay — P tightly bound
categories.moderate_sorption: Moderate clay, neutral pH, moderate organic matter
categories.low_sorption: Sandy, low Fe/Al, high organic matter, or hydroponic — P relatively available

tc_confusion_warnings: Control is the ZERO-SI treatment under the same P conditions — do NOT use +Si as control
In factorial Si x P designs, control is always the no-Si group at matching P level
Root length from WinRHIZO is reported per plant or per pot — note units carefully
Some papers report root:shoot as g/g dry weight, others as cm root length / g shoot — record units
Diameter class data (fine vs coarse roots) should NOT be the primary extraction target — extract total root length first
CO2 experiments may have 4-way combinations (aCO2/eCO2 x +Si/-Si x P source) — extract all combinations
Hydroponic studies use nutrient solution Si concentration (mM); pot/field studies use kg/ha — record both

population.description: Grain crops (cereals and grasses grown for grain)

benchmark.notes: No published meta-analysis on Si x root architecture in grain crops exists — this is a novel synthesis

inclusion_criteria: Grain crop species (wheat, rice, barley, maize, sorghum, millet, oat, rye)
At least one root morphology metric reported (length, area, diameter, tips, volume, root:shoot)
Quantitative data with mean and some measure of variance (SD, SE, LSD, CI) OR extractable from figure
exclusion_criteria: Root data reported only as composite index with no raw morphological metric
No variance data and not extractable from figure

subgroup_analyses.primary: P source type (soluble vs FePO4 vs hydroxyapatite vs rock phosphate vs P-deficient)
secondary: Study type (hydroponic vs pot vs field)
subgroup_analyses.notes: The primary subgroup analysis tests whether Si effect on root architecture differs by P source type — this is the core scientific question linking to the greenhouse experiment on hydroxyapatite vs FePO4 in wheat
